parts.title: From Problem to Solution
parts.html: In the last lesson, you found three big threats to Florida's ecosystems: pollution, invasive species, and habitat loss. People caused many of these problems, and people are now designing solutions. That's what engineers do. They ask a question about a real problem, investigate what is causing it, and design something to help. Then they test it to see if it works.

parts.title: The Engineering Design Process
parts.html: Engineers follow five steps: define the problem, research, design, test, and improve. Before they build anything, they list the criteria (what the design must do) and the constraints (limits like cost, size, and materials). Skipping a step usually means the design fails, so good engineers take their time and check their work at every step.

parts.title: Real Engineers, Real Florida
parts.html:
In the early 1990s, engineers built 24 wildlife crossings and changed 12 bridges along 40 miles of I-75, with tall fences that guide animals to them. To check their work, scientists collect evidence: observations from trail cameras and counts of animals hit by cars.

In the 1970s, only about 20 to 30 panthers were left. Today, scientists estimate about 120 to 230 adults. Crossings are one of several things helping them.

wow.title: A River Put Back
wow.alt: White wading birds gathered in shallow water beside a grassy marsh, seen from the air
wow.caption: Wading birds on the restored Kissimmee River · South Florida Water Management District
wow.html:
Engineers once straightened the Kissimmee River into a canal. The wetlands beside it dried up, and many birds left.

Now engineers have filled parts of the canal, and water flows through the old curves again. Wading birds and fish are coming back.
wow.insetCap: The straight canal, before the repair.

keyIdea: Engineers solve real problems with a design process: define the problem, research, design, test, and improve. Before they build, they list criteria, what the design must do, and constraints, the limits they must work within. In Florida, engineers built wildlife crossings under highways, filter marshes to clean water, and a plan to bring back the Kissimmee River's curves. Evidence from tests, like trail camera observations, shows whether a design works and how to improve it.

quiz.q: What does "criteria" mean in engineering design?

options.t: The limits on your design, like cost or materials
options.miss: Criteria and constraints are easy to mix up. Criteria = what success looks like. Try again!

options.t: The features a solution must have to work well
options.ok: ✅ Exactly! Criteria tell you what success looks like, what the solution must do.

options.t: A test you run on a prototype to find problems
options.miss: Criteria and constraints are easy to mix up. Criteria = what success looks like. Try again!

quiz.q: An engineer designing a water filter must use only natural materials and spend under $20. What does "natural materials and under $20" describe?

options.t: The criteria, what the design must do
options.miss: Think about the word "limits." Constraints are limits. Which answer describes a limit? Try again!

options.t: The prototype, a test version of the filter
options.miss: Think about the word "limits." Constraints are limits. Which answer describes a limit? Try again!

options.t: The constraints, the limits the engineer must work within
options.ok: 🌿 Right! Limits on materials and cost are constraints. The engineer has to work within them.

quiz.q: An engineer tests her wildlife underpass and discovers animals won't use it. What should she do next?

options.t: Give up. If the first design failed, the problem is too hard.
options.miss: Think about the engineering design process. What comes after testing? Try again.

options.t: Start over from scratch with a completely new idea
options.miss: Think about the engineering design process. What comes after testing? Try again.

options.t: Improve the design based on what the test showed
options.ok: ⭐ Yes! Testing shows what needs to change. Then you improve. That's the last step of the process.
